clue.text: Reverse a short distance behind the house

parts.note: to reverse a car is to back it
a yard is a short measure of length, three feet

explanation.surface: A driver edges the car back a little way behind the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' reads as an instruction to turn letters round, but here it is simply a verb meaning to back.
explanation.definitionFit: The yard at the rear of a home lies behind it, so the phrase describes that garden area.

clue.text: How Parliament governs local regulations

explanation.surface: A civics lesson on how Parliament rules and on local rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, BY LAWS: Parliament governs by means of statutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament rules through statutes it passes; separately, the hyphenated word means rules made by a council or local body.

clue.text: Set the price for a pound of rib

parts.note: to set a price for something is to cost it
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A butcher fixes what to charge for a pound of rib meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a joint of meat; the definition is the adjective 'of rib', relating to the ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the ribs, from Latin costa, a rib.

clue.text: Chinese flower the colour of a primrose

explanation.surface: A Chinese bloom shares its shade with the primrose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as 'flow-er', something that flows: a river. China's Huang He is known in English as the Yellow River.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of northern China is called by this colour's name; primroses are pale in this hue.

clue.text: I never rise out of sorts in Paris

indicators.note: feeling out of sorts suggests being jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gloomy Parisian complains of never getting up because they feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is what flows through the French capital, i.e. something found in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The river that runs through the French capital is the obvious watercourse located there.

clue.text: Strike a female swimmer

parts.note: to hit with a bat is to strike
her is the pronoun for a female

explanation.surface: Someone hits a woman who is out swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bathes in the sea or a pool is a swimmer.

clue.text: Finally discover where they print the index

explanation.surface: A reader at last locates where the index is printed.
explanation.walkthrough: An index normally appears at the back of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means lastly or eventually; it also states the position of a book's index, the closing pages.

clue.text: On which a meal may be cooked or served

definitions.text: On which a meal may be cooked or served

parts.words: On which a meal may be cooked or served
parts.note: describes both a stove's heated cooking surface and a warmed dish for serving food

explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both a heated ring on a cooker and a warmed serving dish.

clue.text: Maybe his place is rented

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible alternative arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tenant's home is leased rather than owned.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a tenant who lives in a rented home.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in a place, often as a tenant, occupies a home that may well be leased.

clue.text: Failed to win a point with the lady of his dreams

explanation.surface: A tennis player loses a rally while mooning over his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis 'love' is a score of nothing, so to be beaten at love is to fail to score a point; the second reading is a former sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as tennis, beaten at a nil score means scoring nothing; the phrase also names a sweetheart one has parted from.

clue.text: Conditions across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Weather conditions over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: From Britain, 'across the Atlantic' is America, often called the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means conditions or situations; it is also the common name for the USA, seen from Britain over the ocean.

clue.text: It is needed to open war manoeuvres by the beginning of the year

indicators.note: military manoeuvres move things about, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An army needs something to begin war exercises at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges OPEN and WAR to WEAPONR; 'the beginning of' year adds Y. The definition is just 'It', the thing needed: arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms collectively are the thing an army requires before fighting, which the pronoun stands for here.

clue.text: He had consumed alcohol, but is no longer sick

parts.note: taken as written
ale'd, playfully, means having drunk beer

explanation.surface: A man had been drinking, but has recovered from illness.
explanation.walkthrough: ALED is a playful coinage, 'ale'd', having had ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cured of an illness has recovered and is well again.

clue.text: Retire drunk and have a good night

parts.note: to retire for the night is to go to sleep
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Going to bed tipsy and enjoying a sound night's rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a bedtime farewell wishing someone restful slumber.

clue.text: He gave Napoleon the boot

parts.note: the duke who defeated the French emperor at Waterloo, whose name also became a rubber boot

explanation.definitionFit: The British duke beat Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815, and the knee-high rubber boot is named after him.

clue.text: Don't destroy the garden plot to accommodate guest

parts.note: to spare something is to not destroy it
a bed is a plot of garden for flowers

explanation.surface: A gardener is urged not to ruin the flower patch to make room for a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer's purpose: an extra bed for a visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra bed kept in a guest room exists to provide a visitor with somewhere to sleep.

clue.text: Soldiers turn up a group of marine creatures while training

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the soldiers' letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
a school is a group of fish or dolphins

explanation.surface: Troops arrive at a shoal of fish during an exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' looks like arriving, but in a down clue it reverses TA to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in education or a class means receiving instruction, as a pupil does.

clue.text: Clearly the bowler is not in form and not in tune

definitions.text: Clearly the bowler is not in form

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is out of form and singing flat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler bowls on the pitch; one 'off' it is literally not playing. The second sense is a musical note out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, away from the cricket strip; in music the phrase describes notes sung or played slightly flat or sharp.

clue.text: One who discovers a way of homing onto a target

explanation.surface: A guide finds a route by locking onto the objective.
explanation.walkthrough: In wartime a pathfinder was an aircraft that marked targets for bombers following it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an explorer who finds a route; it also describes aircraft or devices that guide others onto a target.

clue.text: Monk sets nothing on decoration and personal adornment

parts.note: BRO is short for brother, a title for a monk
O is the figure zero, nothing
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British decoration

explanation.surface: A monk places nothing on the ornaments of his habit.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin worn on clothing is an ornamental piece of jewellery.

clue.text: War doctor in his usual attire

indicators.note: the doctor is placed in his attire, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coat is everyday outer wear
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An army doctor wears his ordinary clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a standard abbreviation for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting between forces is warfare, the noun meaning armed conflict.

clue.text: Don't retire from the space laboratory!

explanation.surface: A plea not to leave the orbiting lab.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a crew aboard a space station stays up in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid going to bed is to remain awake late; astronauts in orbit literally remain aloft.

clue.text: Crepe I cooked according to its instructions

indicators.note: cooking something can mean falsifying or altering it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pancake made by following the directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' fits the kitchen surface but here signals rearranging CREPE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook follows a set of directions for preparing a dish.

clue.text: Embark on a career as a top-class solicitor

parts.note: a star performer is top-class
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: Beginning working life as a leading lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a journey or profession is to set off on it.

clue.text: It's a stain to be stoned

parts.note: a blot is an ink stain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being high on drugs is a blemish on one's record.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for heavily intoxicated or drunk.

clue.text: Say farewell into the bargain!

indicators.note: the instruction to say it means the word is spoken and heard

parts.note: a goodbye is a farewell

explanation.surface: Bid someone adieu and a bargain too.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a goodbye' sounds the same as the answer; 'into the' joins wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase that is worth more than its price is a bargain.

clue.text: Where the oracle heartened Diana by cryptic help

indicators.note: heartened means given a heart, so the scrambled letters fill the middle of Diana's short name

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: At a famous oracle, a woman named Diana is cheered by obscure assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' and 'heartened' both look like surface description of Diana's mood; Di is the familiar short form of her name, and the oracle at the shrine was the Pythia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek shrine of Apollo, home of the Pythia, was the most famous seat of prophecy.

clue.text: Descriptive of Hillary on Everest

parts.note: Edmund Hillary reached the summit of the world's highest mountain in 1953

explanation.definitionFit: Hillary stood on the summit of the highest peak, the very highest point possible.
